questions.problem:
Describe the set $S=\{5,6,7,...,50\}$ using a conditional definition.

$$
S=\{x\in {{field-1}}\,:\,{{field-2}}\le x\le {{field-3}}\}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The set $S$ contains all natural numbers between $5$ and $50$ (including $5$ and $50$).

Therefore, the set can be written as

$$
S=\{x\in N\,:\,5\le x\le 50\}.
$$

**Note**: This definition is not unique. For example:

- We can write $x\in Z.$ This gives

$$
S=\{x\in Z\,:\,5\le x\le 50\}.
$$

- We can write $4<x<51.$ This gives

$$
S=\{x\in N\,:\,4<x<51\},
$$

or, writing $x\in Z$ as before, we have

$$
S=\{x\in Z\,:\,4<x<51\}.
$$

questions.problem:
Describe the set $S=\{…,3,6,12,24,48,...\}$ using a constructive definition.

*Hint: Take ${a}_{1}=6$ in the sequence that generates the elements of $S.$*

$$
S=\{{{field-1}}\,:\,n\in {{field-2}}\}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the elements of our set

$$
…,\,3,\,6,\,12,\,24,\,48,\,…
$$

form a two-way infinite geometric sequence with a common ratio $r=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =2 \\  & =\frac{6}{3} \\  & =\frac{12}{6} \\  & =\frac{24}{12} \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, setting  ${a}_{1}=6,$ the $n$th term ${a}_{n}$ of our sequence for $n\in Z$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =6\cdot {2}^{n-1} \\  & =6\cdot {2}^{n}\cdot {2}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{6}{2}\cdot {2}^{n} \\  & =3\cdot {2}^{n}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can define our set using a constructive definition as follows:

$$
S=\{3\cdot {2}^{n}\,:\,n\in Z\}
$$

$$
questions.worked_solution:
The set $S$ contains all integer numbers between $-6$ and $12$ (including $-6$ and $12$).

Therefore, the set can be written as

$$
S=\{x\in Z\,:\,-6\le x\le 12\}.
$$

**Note**: This definition is not unique. For example:

- We can write $-7<x<13.$ This gives

$$

$$

$$

The given set contains the roots $x\in R$ of some cubic polynomial $p(x).$

Since the cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=-3,$ ${x}_{2}=-\sqrt{5},$ and ${x}_{3}=\sqrt{5},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=3,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =(3)(x-(-3))(x-(-\sqrt{5}))(x-\sqrt{5}) \\  & =3(x+3)(x+\sqrt{5})(x-\sqrt{5}) \\  & =3(x+3)({x}^{2}-\sqrt{5}x+\sqrt{5}x-(\sqrt{5})^{2}) \\  & =3(x+3)({x}^{2}-5) \\  & =3({x}^{3}-5x+3{x}^{2}-15) \\  & =3{x}^{3}+9{x}^{2}-15x-45\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can express the given set as

$$
\{-3,-\sqrt{5},\sqrt{5}\}=\{x\in R\,:\,3{x}^{3}+9{x}^{2}-15x-45=0\}.
$$
